findings.where: Page header (h1 'Best Hostels in Canggu') against the coming-soon notice at the foot of the page
findings.fault: The heading promises a list of the best hostels in Canggu, but the page has none. The only place that says listings are not live yet is the last block, after the whole guide. A visitor from search spends the page waiting for a list that never comes.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker who searched 'best hostels Canggu' to pick one. They feel the title tricked them and leave without trusting the site. The founder would object too, since honesty is the brand's stated product.

findings.where: 'Good for' section: all twelve tags (First-time surfers, Remote workers, Long stays, Meeting people, Yoga, Nightlife, Budget, Cafés, Couples, Solo travellers, Scooter riders, Sunsets)
findings.fault: parts.txt shows these are static facts. Each one is drawn as a bold filled pill with a contrasting edge, which makes them look like filter chips or buttons. Tapping does nothing. The random colours (pink, purple, red, coral, yellow, teal) also suggest categories that don't exist, so the eye looks for a meaning that isn't there.
findings.who_objects: A visitor on a phone who taps 'First-time surfers' expecting to filter or jump to hostels, and gets nothing. The rules give the chip shape to selectable filters, and these tags borrow it.

findings.fault: The tags use colours outside the brand palette: magenta, purple, pink-red and a coral-like red ground. Coral is meant only for the one call to action per view. The colours carry no information, and together they make the calmest part of the guide the loudest.
findings.who_objects: The founder and anyone holding the brand sheet. Coral as decoration and off-palette hues break 'every colour has one job', and an orange-red field moves toward Hostelworld's look.

findings.fault: The heading is set in turquoise, italic and underlined, so it looks like a link. parts.txt shows it is static. None of the other section headings has this look.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who clicks it expecting more on Canggu's vibe and gets nothing. The rules keep the link colour and the underline for links only.

findings.where: Coming-soon notice near the foot of the page
findings.fault: The notice is white text on a saturated red ground. That reads as an error or a warning, when it is a neutral 'listings coming soon' message. The rules file names this block as the interior announcement, which sits on the ink night ground.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who sees an alarm-red box and thinks something failed or the page is broken. The founder too, since the rules file fixes this block's ground.

findings.where: Nav 'How we rank' and footer 'Privacy', 'Terms', 'How we rank', 'Report content'; nav 'Destinations'
findings.fault: parts.txt shows the nav and footer links point back to this same page, so they go nowhere. 'Destinations' points to #destinations, and no destinations section is visible on the page.
findings.who_objects: A visitor checking how hostels are ranked, or reading the privacy terms before trusting the site, ends up back where they started. That is the trust check a pre-launch site most needs to pass.

findings.fault: 'We'll show direct-booking options alongside the major booking sites so you can compare and choose' promises a side-by-side comparison with the booking sites. The project's terms forbid showing their prices or availability for comparison, so the page promises something the product cannot deliver.
findings.who_objects: The founder, because of the OTA terms. Later, a visitor who expects a price comparison and doesn't get one.

findings.where: End of the guide, after the coming-soon notice
findings.fault: There is no next step anywhere on the page. A visitor who decides Canggu suits them can't see other destinations, get told when listings open, or go anywhere but the footer. The page just stops.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker planning their next stop who is ready to act and has nothing to act on, so the visit is wasted.

findings.where: Section headings: 'Surf', 'Vibe', 'Good for', 'What to look for'
findings.fault: Four sibling sections get four different heading treatments: a plain h2, an italic underlined turquoise one, a plain h2, and a small tracked uppercase eyebrow. 'What to look for' is half the page's job (what to look for in a hostel), yet it gets the weakest heading, and its body is a single sentence.
findings.who_objects: A visitor scanning on a phone for what to look for in a hostel. That section is the easiest to miss and the thinnest, so the brief's second question is barely answered.

findings.where: First screen, top of the page
findings.fault: The page opens on plain sand with a text heading and no hero ground, illustration or any of the brand's energy. The rules file puts destination-page top banners in the loud marketing zone. As it stands, the first screen reads like a plain document.
findings.who_objects: The founder, whose named enemy is sterile. A first-time visitor gets no feeling of the place or the brand before reading.

findings.where: Body text throughout: intro, Surf, Vibe, What to look for, and the coming-soon notice (worst at phone width)
findings.fault: The text is justified, which opens wide, uneven gaps between words. It is worst in the phone notice ('MantaHostels   is   launching   across') and the phone intro, where it makes reading stop and start.
findings.who_objects: A phone reader mid-transit, who reads more slowly and loses their place in the uneven lines.

findings.where: Desktop layout: text column against the tag rows and notice
findings.fault: The guide text sits in a narrow left column with the right two-thirds empty. The tags and the notice then run full width, and the notice's text stays in the left half of a full-width box, leaving a large blank red area. The page has no consistent column.
findings.who_objects: A desktop planner. The empty right side and the half-filled red box look unfinished.

findings.fault: The heading is in Title Case, but the brand voice is sentence case.
findings.who_objects: The founder, because the rule is in the brand voice.

findings.fault: The page shows no reviews, sources or any sign of who wrote the guide or why to trust it, apart from an email address in the footer. None can be invented, because the project holds no proof yet.
findings.who_objects: A first-time visitor deciding whether this unknown site's take on Canggu is worth trusting.
